CDC ART Surveillance 2002. The US series in the frame now runs 2000-2018 with only scattered gaps — effectively the whole national exposure record.

AYA cancer incidence, Japan.

POPULATION TRENDS and live birth rates by ART treatment strategy over 12 years in Australia. Population-level and strategy-specific — it links the clinical practice change to the aggregate birth count, which is the join arm 1 usually skips.
Birth defects in singleton vs multiple ART births, Japan.
Sperm motility video analysis.

**JAMA: trends and outcomes for DONOR OOCYTE cycles, US 2000-2010.** Donor eggs are the one treatment that actually breaks the age-fecundity constraint P4 models, and the UK record in batch 1 separates them for exactly that reason. Central to the recovery arm, not peripheral.
Obesity, ART and preterm birth.
State-level LIFETIME infertility estimates from BRFSS. Wall 4, but state-level is the unit arm 2's mandate designs use, so it may serve as a covariate.

**Japanese nationwide survey of oocyte and ovarian-tissue cryopreservation with REPRODUCTIVE OUTCOMES, compared across survey waves.** Outcomes rather than attitudes, at national scale. Indication is not split in the abstract — a Wall 5 residue case that has to be resolved at full text.
Obstetric care quality in sub-arctic Norway.
Sperm banking among adolescents with cancer.

**Reproductive outcomes after breast cancer WITH vs WITHOUT preservation.** A treated-vs-untreated birth comparison — the right design, in Wall 5's medical population. Worth flagging to whoever writes the preservation section: the oncofertility literature has the comparison design that the elective literature lacks.
FSH dosing calculator study.
Ovarian cancer survival with preservation.
Fertility-sparing surgery in ovarian cancer.
Fertility decision-making in cancer patients.
Maternal outcomes in multiple pregnancies, Tanzania.
Regional oncofertility network, Japan.
Health of IVF-conceived children.
Genome-wide haplotyping in PGT-M.
Hospital costs of multiple-birth children and ART's role.

**TURKEY's 2010 ART legislation favouring single embryo transfer, evaluated nationwide.** Another regulation-as-shock record; outcome is neonatal, so it routes to A.12/Wall 2, but the legislative variation is real and A.17 should know it exists.
Treatment and preterm birth among subfertile women. Note again the design: subfertile-untreated as the comparison.
Breast cancer survivors at risk of infertility.
Japanese cryopreservation survey for cancer patients.
Heparin in assisted conception.
ART and ovarian cancer risk.

**Contribution of ART AND OVULATION-INDUCING DRUGS to triplet and higher-order multiples, US 1980-1997.** The fifth OI-separating record. A.12's chapter should receive this whole cluster as a group: the ovulation-induction channel is separately quantified across five studies and is the channel single-embryo-transfer policy cannot touch.

ART and birth defects, separating subfertility and multiples.

Perinatal outcomes of ART twins; notes ART causes ~18% of US multiple births.

Effect of the 2017 Japanese preservation GUIDELINES on practice. A guideline-as-shock design, in Wall 5's medical half.
Tubal factor infertility and perinatal risk.
Endometriosis, ART and adverse pregnancy outcome.
Supplementary-materials record on infant mortality trends. Paratext.

**Within-sibship analysis separating PARENTAL from TREATMENT contributions to perinatal health.** Wall 2 by outcome, but methodologically the best answer in the frame to 'is it the treatment or the people who get it' — the same confound arm 1's counterfactual faces. Worth borrowing the design argument.
Birth outcomes in women with melanoma.
Time to pregnancy, fresh vs freeze-all.

**Sociodemographic profile of women seeking ELECTIVE egg freezing WHEN PUBLICLY FINANCED.** With the Japanese municipal programme and the French publicly funded cohort, P5 now has three public-subsidy settings — which is the exposure PI call 2 needs and which the recon probe suggested did not exist.
No abstract. PRE- AND POST-INTERVENTION analysis of awareness of age-related fertility and elective preservation among clinicians-in-training.
No abstract. Obstetricians' approach to counselling on reproductive ageing and elective preservation.
Ethics of social egg freezing. Normative, and it names the non-medical indication explicitly.
Danish and Israeli students on WHO SHOULD PAY for egg freezing — the financing question from the demand side, in two countries with opposite public-funding regimes.

**PLANNED OOCYTE CRYOPRESERVATION, 10-15 YEAR FOLLOW-UP: RETURN RATES AND CYCLE OUTCOMES.** The longest follow-up of elective freezing in the frame and the single most decisive P5 record: return rate is the parameter that determines whether egg freezing produces any births at all. Highest priority in the cell.
No abstract. Reproductive choices and likelihood of freezing in the elective era.
No abstract. Public support for elective oocyte cryopreservation.
